evidence.note: After write truncation, agent runs py_compile and boots the service with curl smoke tests (health, customer). It diagnoses uncertainty about whether the file was written cleanly and verifies before proceeding — root-cause checking rather than barreling ahead.

Step 6 is the main adaptation: agent recognizes that the stripe-python SDK sends Basic auth (not Bearer), so its idempotency cache-key extraction was built on a wrong assumption; it patches Basic-auth handling plus related gaps (product/price/webhook modify routes, list-limit robustness, refunds by payment_intent). This is a contract-level insight propagated across endpoints — but it is anticipatory ('likely verifier edge cases'), not driven by an observed failing SDK round-trip.

After applying the patch batch and restarting the service, the agent jumps straight to Submit (steps 7-8) without re-running the SDK/curl checks against the patched behavior — so the correction is not verified, and the horizon ends without evidence-driven iteration on the deep traps (webhook re-signing, idempotency locking, fuller state machine).

reasoning: The agent shows one genuine mid-course correction — realizing stripe-python uses Basic (not Bearer) auth and reworking idempotency key extraction, propagated to a few related endpoints — which reaches toward the level-8 'divergence as contract signal' idea. But it never actually round-trips the real SDK to surface contradictions; the fixes are a single speculative patch batch, applied and then left unverified before an immediate submit. That is closer to diagnosing and fixing a case then moving on (level 5) than to sustained, evidence-driven correction across the horizon (level 8).
